=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:873-895 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The anchor parser in `scan_content_line` accepts only a `path:line` token, or a `FILE:` line followed by a `LINE:` line. It misses the standard reviewer shape `File: <path>` plus `Line or code reference: <ref>` (and `Code:`): the `LINE:` regex at line 888 does not match it, and the blank-line reset then clears `pending_file`, so no anchor is recorded.
  WHY: From round 3, when two reviewers raise a finding in the standard shape and the consolidator quotes only one of them, cnt=1 < min_reviewers=2. The finding is demoted to `advisory-lone`, stripped of CURRENT_CODE and SUGGESTED_APPROACH, and the editor is told "Make no edits for them". This breaks "Round 3, a finding raised by two reviewers: blocks" in the unsafe direction. The last run's change at lines 1048-1058 made this parser the only path that decides the count. All reviewers who stated a severity said MAJOR.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1497-1508 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The resume-stub arm of the editor directive condition (`[ -s "${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_convergence_advisory.txt" ] || grep -qs '^=== ADVISORY ISSUE ' "${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_issues.txt"`) prints the "NOT blocking ... Make no edits for them" instruction without checking `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_ENABLED`.
  WHY: Suppose an operator sets `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_ENABLED=false` after an enabled partial run. The same-head resume restores `review_issues.txt` with `=== ADVISORY ISSUE` stubs, the classifier and stub-rewriter return early, and the directive still renders. The switch-off contract, "every decision is identical to today's", therefore fails on the rollback path. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT (rare, needs a switch flip during a resume window); minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it MAJOR. The highest is used.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:947-1058 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `process_block`, the FLAGGED_BY name-matching loop was removed, but `flagged = value_of(l)` and `named[s] = 0` are still written and never read. `named` is no longer in the local signature, so it leaks as an implicit global awk array.
  WHY: There is no correctness impact. It is dead per-finding gawk work plus an unintended global left over from the last run's refactor. Reviewers who stated a severity said NIT.
- agents.d/10056-review-convergence-rule.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fragment says the round falls back to `AUTOFIX_ITERATION`; README.md:2910 and changelog.d/10056-review-convergence-rule.md:1 say the same. But `review_convergence_load_config` falls back to `${ITERATION}`: scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:765 per gemini, scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:748 per minimax.
  WHY: Operators configuring `REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_FROM_ROUND` may be misled. minimax itself notes that scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:1321 sets `ITERATION_RAW="${AUTOFIX_ITERATION:-${ITERATION:-1}}"`, so the docs are functionally right. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash checked this claim and rejected it as accurate docs.

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A lone finding below that bar is written to the ledger as advisory, shown in the PR's review comment under its own heading, and passed to the review-blocked judge. It is never dropped silently."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh "# Review convergence rule (issue #10056)" block (renderer, lines 246-291), and/or the scripts/review_autofix_step_partial_finalize.sh runtime artifact persistence list (lines 372-385)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/review_autofix_step_partial_finalize.sh:372-385 persists `review_issues.txt` (lines 157 and 379) but not `review_convergence_advisory.txt`. Same-head restore copies only persisted artifacts (scripts/review_autofix_step_restore_partial_resume.sh:175-181). The "Not blocking (one reviewer)" heading in scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:251-253 and 283-291 renders only when the TSV is non-empty, so on a resumed run the PR comment loses the heading and rows. The renderer has no fallback to the `=== ADVISORY ISSUE` stubs, unlike the editor prompt. No test covers the comment on a resume. The prior editor deferred this as outside files_touched (CONSOLIDATOR_OVERRIDDEN: 005). Sonnet notes that post_editor_summary.sh is in the files_touched grant, so a fix there that rebuilds bullets from the stubs needs no change to partial_finalize.
- requirement: "A failed CI check on the head blocks in every round." / "A CI failure on the head always blocks."
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh review_convergence_classify
  confidence=4

The guarantee rests only on the prompt sentence in scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1507 (gemini cites line 1511). The PR author recorded this as deliberate (CONSOLIDATOR_OVERRIDDEN: 010). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly skipped this gap: the head gate and final CI are untouched, as asserted by test_review_convergence_ci_gates_untouched.
- requirement: "Round 3, a finding raised by two reviewers: blocks." The reviewer count must come from the per-reviewer files.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_review_issue_ledger.py, next to test_convergence_two_verified_reviewers_block, plus the parser fix in scan_content_line
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: Every two-reviewer fixture writes the second reviewer either as `FILE: src/module.py\nLINE: 4` or as a verbatim evidence quote. No fixture uses the reviewer prompt's own `File:` / `Line or code reference:` shape, and the parser does not support that shape.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:review_convergence_classify, gawk function scan_content_line (mid-line path:line loop, FILE: regex, `match(line, /^[[:space:]]*[Ll][Ii][Nn][Ee]:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+)/, l)`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The support check finds anchors only as a `path:line` token, or as `FILE:` followed directly by `LINE:`. It misses the prompt's `File:` + `Line or code reference:` shape, which scripts/review_floor_rules.sh already parses at lines 467 and 478. In that shape the blank line clears pending_file, so no anchor is recorded.
  WHY: From round 3, a finding from two reviewers using the standard shape with a paraphrasing consolidator gets cnt=1 < min_reviewers=2. It is demoted to `advisory-lone` and stubbed, and the editor is told "Make no edits for them", which is the unsafe direction. The only two-reviewer fixture uses `FILE:`/`LINE:`. Suggested fix: about 4 lines in scan_content_line matching `^[[:space:]]*(line or code reference|code)[[:space:]]*:`, plus a fixture.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:CONSOLIDATOR + LEDGER CONTEXT directive condition `$(if [ -s "${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_convergence_advisory.txt" ] || grep -qs '^=== ADVISORY ISSUE ' "${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_issues.txt"; then` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The stub-based branch never checks REVIEW_CONVERGENCE_ENABLED. A resumed run can restore stubs, because partial_finalize persists review_issues.txt (lines 157 and 379).
  WHY: With the kill switch flipped to false between a partial run and its resume, the editor is still told "NOT blocking ... Make no edits for them". This breaks "With the switch off, every decision is identical to today's". Rare, but it is the rollback path. Suggested fix: a 1-line case guard.
- scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh:process_block local list, `named[s] = 0`, `flagged = value_of(l)` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `flagged` extraction and the `named[s] = 0` writes are left with no reader, and `named` is now an implicit global array.
  WHY: Nothing breaks; it is dead work plus a stray global. Suggested fix: delete 3 lines.
- (Note: the reviewer rejected the pass-1 docs claim about the `AUTOFIX_ITERATION` fallback. scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh line 1321 sets `ITERATION_RAW="${AUTOFIX_ITERATION:-${ITERATION:-1}}"`, and test_convergence_round_falls_back_to_autofix_iteration covers it.)
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "A lone finding below that bar is written to the ledger as advisory, shown in the PR's review comment under its own heading, and passed to the review-blocked judge. It is never dropped silently."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh, "# Review convergence rule (issue #10056)" block (in files_touched)
  Evidence of absence: The heading renders only when `${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_convergence_advisory.txt` is non-empty. scripts/review_autofix_step_partial_finalize.sh persists review_issues.txt (lines 157 and 379) but not the TSV, and the renderer has no stub fallback. Suggested fix: build bullets from the stubs' FILE, LINES, LENS, SEVERITY, CONVERGENCE_REVIEWERS, CONVERGENCE_ROUND and SUMMARY lines via clean(). The ledger and judge notes still record these findings.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "Round 3, a finding raised by two reviewers: blocks." The reviewer count must come from the per-reviewer files.
  Expected change site: tests/test_review_issue_ledger.py next to test_convergence_two_verified_reviewers_block, plus the scan_content_line parser fix
  Evidence of absence: Two-reviewer fixtures use only `FILE: src/module.py\nLINE: 4` or verbatim quotes, never `File:` / `Line or code reference:`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- (Skipped gap: "A failed CI check on the head blocks in every round". Head gate and final CI are untouched, as asserted by test_review_convergence_ci_gates_untouched.)
- HARDENING: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh clean() in the "Not blocking (one reviewer)" awk block. Bare `https://...` URLs and `#123` references survive (the test asserts "see xhttps://e.invalid" is kept), and GitHub autolinks both. Suggested fix: add `gsub(/[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//, "", s)` and `gsub(/#/, "", s)` and update the test; about 3 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
